report.tagline: An AI notepad for meetings that listens through your computer, with no bot joining the call, and turns your rough notes into clean summaries.
report.simpleSummary: Granola is a notes app for meetings. You open it during a call and jot a few rough notes. Granola quietly listens to the audio on your laptop or phone, and when the meeting ends it combines your notes with what was said into a tidy summary. Unlike most rivals, no robot 'notetaker' joins the call, which makes it feel natural and polite.

overview.whatItDoes: Granola is a desktop and iPhone app that captures meeting audio, transcribes it and writes notes. It works with any call app (Zoom, Google Meet, Teams, Slack) and in-person meetings, because it records the device audio directly. It is moving from personal notes to a company-wide 'memory' of meetings that teams and AI tools can search.
howItWorks: Granola sees your calendar and pops up when a meeting starts.
It transcribes your computer's microphone and speaker audio; no bot joins the call.
You type short notes during the meeting if you want.
Afterward, AI expands your notes into a full summary using the transcript, in your format or a template.
Chat with one meeting or all past meetings, for example 'What did the client say about pricing?'
Share notes to Slack, Notion or a CRM, and use shared team folders and APIs for company knowledge.
overview.valueProposition: Great meeting notes without a bot in the call and without breaking your focus.

businessModel.summary: Granola sells subscriptions. Individuals start free, then pay when they hit limits. Teams and companies pay per user per month for sharing, admin controls and security. Growth is bottom-up: one person loves it, then their team and company buy it.

revenueStreams.detail: About $14 per user a month for unlimited meetings and team features.
Higher price for admin, security and APIs.
For users who outgrow free limits.

businessModel.pricing: Free plan with limited meeting history. Business about $14 per user a month. Enterprise about $35 per user a month or custom. Prices from granola.ai and may change.
costDrivers: Transcription and AI model costs for every meeting
Engineering for Mac, Windows and iPhone apps
businessModel.unitEconomics: A Business user pays $14 a month. If they have 40 meetings a month, transcription and AI summaries might cost $2 to 4. So each paying user is likely profitable with a 70% or so gross margin. Since growth comes mostly from word of mouth, the cost to win a user is low, which makes each customer very valuable over time.

howTheyGetUsers: Word of mouth among founders, investors and tech workers
Shared note links that show the product to others
Posts on X and LinkedIn praising the experience
Being bot-free means no awkward exposure, but users recommend it
whatBringsUsersBack: Every meeting triggers Granola via the calendar
Past notes become more valuable over time
Chat across meetings encourages regular search
growth.moat: Granola's moat is a simple, loved experience and the growing memory of each user's meetings. The more meetings you store, the harder it is to leave. But big players like Zoom, Microsoft and Google can build similar features, so Granola must win on quality and becoming the company's meeting knowledge base.

northStar.metric: Weekly meetings with notes that are opened, shared or searched later
northStar.why: Notes create value when people use them after the meeting. This north star metric shows real value, and it grows with both meeting volume and how useful the notes are. Guardrail metrics make sure growth does not come at the cost of trust, safety or margins.

pmLessons: Small UX choices can define a product. Removing the bot made Granola feel different from every rival.
Keep the user in control. Expanding the user's own notes builds trust.
Bottom-up growth works. Delight individuals and teams follow.
Data builds stickiness. A library of past meetings makes leaving harder.
Watch for platform risk. Zoom, Microsoft and Google can copy features.

interviewQuestions.question: Granola does not send a bot into meetings. What are the trade-offs?
interviewQuestions.hint: Pros: natural, polite, works everywhere. Cons: consent, no video, depends on device audio. Suggest mitigations.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you take Granola from individuals to enterprises?
interviewQuestions.hint: Map buyer needs: security, admin, consent, integrations. Use bottom-up usage data to sell. Measure seats per company.

interviewQuestions.question: Zoom makes AI notes free for all users. How should Granola respond?
interviewQuestions.hint: Focus on cross-platform, in-person, quality and memory. Consider pricing and partnerships.

interviewQuestions.question: Define a north star for Granola.
interviewQuestions.hint: Meetings with notes used after. Break into captured, quality, reuse and team adoption.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you design Granola for Indian teams?
interviewQuestions.hint: Hindi and Hinglish transcription, low price, WhatsApp sharing, mobile focus. Test with startups.
